content.text: Repo is public, I have admin, no protection and no rulesets exist. CI already runs `lint`, `build`, `test` (ubuntu/macos/windows) and `statusline`, and everything lands via PR — but all recent PRs were self-merged by you, so the approval requirement is the one choice that actually changes your workflow.

questions.question: How strict should main branch protection be?

options.label: PR + CI, no approvals (Recommended)
options.description: Require a PR to merge, require lint/build/test checks to pass, block force pushes and branch deletion. 0 required approvals so you can still self-merge. Repo admins can bypass.

options.label: PR + CI + 1 approval
options.description: Same as above, but every PR needs one approving review. You could no longer self-merge without another collaborator reviewing (admins can still bypass).

options.label: Minimal
options.description: Only block force pushes and branch deletion. Direct pushes to main stay allowed, no PR or CI gate. Clears the GitHub banner with the least friction.

content.text:
Done — `main` now reports `protected: true`, so the GitHub banner will clear.

**What I created:** a repository ruleset named `main` (ruleset ID `20303173`), targeting `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`, enforcement `active`. Rulesets rather than classic branch protection, since that's GitHub's current mechanism and it satisfies the same banner.

**Rules in effect:**
- **Pull request required** — no direct pushes to `main`. `required_approving_review_count: 0`, so you can still self-merge your own PRs; merge/squash/rebase all allowed.
- **Required status checks** — all 9 jobs from `.github/workflows/test.yml`, pinned to the GitHub Actions app so a third party can't spoof a green context: `lint`, `build`/`test` on ubuntu+macos+windows, `statusline` on ubuntu+macos. "Require branches to be up to date" is off, so you won't have to rebase every PR when `main` moves.
- **Block force pushes** (`non_fast_forward`) and **block branch deletion**.

**Bypass:** repository admins (role ID 5) have `bypass_mode: always`. That's the escape hatch for an emergency push — but it also means the protection is advisory for you specifically, since you have admin. If you'd rather it bind you too, I can drop the bypass actor; you'd then need a PR with green CI for every change to `main`, including your own.

One thing to watch: `windows-latest` is in the required set. If that job is ever flaky or gets removed from the matrix, PRs will sit unmergeable until the check reports — the required contexts are matched by exact name, so renaming a job in the workflow silently blocks merges until the ruleset is updated to match.
